summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with advanced multiple sclerosis, neurogenic bladder with a suprapubic catheter, and a history of recurrent multidrug-resistant urinary tract infections, was admitted with fever, tachycardia, and hypoxia. He was found to have multifocal left-sided pneumonia and acute hypoxic respiratory failure, requiring brief ICU admission and oxygen support. A CT scan revealed small bilateral pulmonary emboli, prompting initiation of apixaban. Blood cultures were negative, but urine culture grew a multidrug-resistant non-fermenter, leading to targeted treatment with meropenem for 7 days. He developed a troponin rise consistent with type 2 myocardial infarction due to sepsis and hypoxia, managed conservatively. A video swallow study showed intermittent penetration without aspiration, allowing continuation of a soft diet with chin tuck. His baclofen pump had adequate supply, and he was discharged home with services on apixaban, home medications including nitrofurantoin for UTI prophylaxis, and follow-up plans for urology, infectious disease, neurology, and outpatient imaging.
